title.narrative: Improving Fiscal Sustainability Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed Improving Fiscal Sustainability Program will help the Government of Nauru strengthen gender-responsive fiscal sustainability by implementing policy and institutional reforms to (i) enhance fiscal and debt management, (ii) improve the governance of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), (iii) advance social protection systems; (iv) increase women's economic participation; and (v) reduce gender-based violence (GBV). The program will support key operational priorities of Strategy 2030 of the Asian Development Bank (ADB): addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities, accelerating progress in gender equality, and strengthening governance and institutional capacity. The program aligns with all three objectives in ADB's Pacific Approach, 2021-2025: preparing for and responding to shocks, delivering sustainable services, and supporting inclusive growth. The program was designed knowing that Nauru is both a small island developing state and a fragile and conflict-affected situation. Following the Joint Multilateral Development Bank Methodological Principles for Assessment of Paris Agreement Alignment of New Operations, the operation has been assessed as aligned with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Oct 01, 2020 - Jan 31, 2024

description.narrative:
Action 1: To ensure that the government's debt is sustainable, (i) the government approved a DAP, and (ii) as part of implementing the DAP, the government reduced the stock of debt by legally settling an outstanding dispute with Firebird on a series of Samurai bonds with face value and accrued interest of approximately A$121.7 million. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 2: To improve debt management arrangements and preserve debt sustainability, (i) cabinet approved the MTDS (2023-2028); and (ii) the Department of Finance published the MTDS on its website. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 3: To promote debt transparency, (i) cabinet approved a financial instruction on state liabilities; and (ii) the Department of Finance disclosed its stock of public debt in the FY2022 and FY2023 annual budgets. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 4: To improve public financial management processes, including the budget cycle, the Government completed a PEFA public financial management assessment and supplementary gender budgeting assessment. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 5: To improve customs administration, including increasing revenues, reducing customs processing and clearance times, and improving the integrity and quality of service delivery, (i) the government installed the ASYCUDA World system; and (ii) cabinet approved regulations under the Customs Act (2014). Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 6: To help manage the financial costs associated with climate change, strengthen adaptation to climate change and related disaster risks, and promote climate resilient development, (i) cabinet approved a climate change policy that supports the integration of climate change responses into key aspects of Nauru life; (ii) the Parliament of Nauru passed an “Environmental Management and Climate Change Act”, which establishes a Climate Change and Environment Protection Fund to help finance activities to address the impacts of climate change; and (iii) the Government of Nauru submitted to the UNFCCC in line with international commitments a gender-responsive Updated Nationally Determined Contribution for the period through 2030. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 1: To ensure that the government's debt is sustainable and as part of the government's approved DAP, the government will take measures to reduce the stock of debt, including by settling the outstanding liabilities of A$24.4 million following the collapse of the Bank of Nauru. Target date: 2025-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Feb 01, 2024 - Dec 31, 2025

description.narrative:
Policy 1: Fiscal and debt management NA
Action 2: To preserve debt sustainability, the Department of Finance will ensure that no loan guarantees are issued as per the MTDS (2023-2028). Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 3: To continue to promote debt transparency, the Department of Finance will (i) disclose its stock of public debt in the annual budgets for FY2024 and FY2025; and (ii) prepare a fiscal risk report as per the financial instruction on state liabilities for any borrowing requests by SOEs. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 4: To improve public financial management processes, including the budget cycle, the Department of Finance will develop a PFM roadmap and begin implementation of the PFM roadmap, including gender-responsive budget initiatives. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 5: To improve customs administration, including increasing revenues, reducing customs processing and clearance times, and improving the integrity and quality of service delivery, the government will give view-only access to the ASYCUDA World system to government clients. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 6: As part of managing the fiscal risks associated with climate change, (i) cabinet will approve a gender-responsive National Adaptation Plan to strengthen adaptation to climate change and related disaster risks, promote climate resilient development, adhere to international commitments, and include a long-term risk assessment of climate change impacts and associated loss and damage; and (ii) the Department of Finance will operationalize the Climate Change and Environment Protection Fund through regulations or guidance that is published on its website. Target date: 2025-12-31

title.narrative: Policy 2 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Feb 01, 2024 - Dec 31, 2025

description.narrative:
Policy 2: Governance of state-owned enterprises NA
Action 2: To improve the governance of SOEs as required under the Public Enterprises Act (2019) and, as part of implementing the gender-sensitive code of conduct, (i) at least two (2) SOEs (of 9) will adopt a gender policy that includes measurable objectives to achieve gender diversity within their workforce, including management and technical positions; and (ii) cabinet will enact with immediate effect implementing regulations for remuneration of directors of public enterprises to ensure fair and appropriate remuneration based on a robust analytical assessment. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 3: To institutionalize regular reporting and robust corporate governance as required under the Public Enterprises Act (2019), (i) at least five (5) SOEs (of 9) will publish on the Department of Finance's website their Annual Report, which includes gender data and audited financial statements, for the financial year ending 30 June 2025, and (ii) at least five (5) SOEs (of 9) will submit their Statement of Corporate Intent for the period 2024/25 to 2027/28. Target date: 2025-12-31
Action 4: To improve the government's oversight of its SOE portfolio, the PEMU will (i) ensure that Nauru Airlines will include in its Statement of Corporate Intent for the period 2025/26 to 2028/29 a report on its climate change risks and the implications for its operations; and (ii) implement systems to produce regular reporting to the Secretary of Finance and the Minister of Finance on individual SOEs and the SOE portfolio to increase the government's oversight of SOEs and ensure government decision makers are aware of SOE performance issues. Target date: 2025-12-31

Action 1: To protect the most vulnerable people in a fiscally sustainable manner, the Department of Finance published on its website, (i) a Social Protection Strategy (2022-2032) that promotes the fiscal sustainability of existing and future social protection programs, incorporates gender analysis, considers the multidimensional impacts of climate change, and includes reform options to optimize targeting of the poor, vulnerable, and women and girls to improve the effectiveness and financial sustainability of the social protection interventions in Nauru; and (ii) the Nauru Social Protection Digital Roadmap to streamline the administration of social protection programs, minimize errors and ensure that benefits reach the intended recipients in a timely manner, promote transparency, and implement data collection, analysis and utilization of data to track social protection expenditures including sex-disaggregated data to better monitor and report on the performance of Nauru's social protection programs. Target date: 2024-01-31

title.narrative: Policy 2 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Oct 01, 2020 - Jan 31, 2024

description.narrative:
Policy 2: Governance of state-owned enterprises NA
Action 2: To improve the governance of SOEs as required under the Public Enterprises Act (2019), cabinet approved a template for a gender-sensitive code of conduct for SOE boards and employees. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 3: To institutionalize regular reporting and robust corporate governance as required under the Public Enterprises Act (2019), at least three (3) public enterprises published on the Department of Finance's website their (i) Annual Report, which includes sex-disaggregated data and audited financial statements, for the financial year ending 30 June 2022, and (ii) Statement of Corporate Intent. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 4: To improve the government's oversight of its SOE portfolio, as required under the Public Enterprises Act (2019), the Department of Finance operationalized its PEMU (i) by filling all the vacancies (3) in the PEMU, namely the Director and 2 officers; and (ii) introduced new systems and regular reporting to the Secretary of Finance and the Minister of Finance on individual SOEs and the SOE portfolio. In addition, the Minister of Finance directed Nauru Airlines to prepare a framework that reports on climate change risks to its operations, and that report to be part of its Statement of Corporate Intent for the period 2025/26 to 2028/29. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 1: To ensure SOE proposals for financing from the government fits within the government's fiscal strategy and promotes more robust SOE financing requests, the government will confirm that all SOE financing proposals from approval of the “Funding for SOEs and Accountability Reporting” policy until 31 December 2025 are as per the policy. Target date: 2025-12-31

description.narrative:
Policy 3: Fiscally responsible support for vulnerable groups, including women NA
Action 2: To protect vulnerable women and contribute to them being productive members of society, the government strengthened implementation of the Child Protection and Welfare Act (2016) and the Domestic Violence and Family Protection Act (2017) by having the Department of Women's and Social Development Affairs, (i) establish and convene meetings of an intergovernmental mechanism, and (ii) sign a memorandum of understanding with the Nauru Police to ensure effective referral and coordination under the Acts. Target date: 2024-01-31
Action 1: To protect the most vulnerable people in a fiscally sustainable manner, the government will (i) implement the inclusive climate and disaster-responsive Social Protection Strategy (2022-2032) to improve fiscally responsible social welfare provision in Nauru; and (ii) start the implementation of the social protection management information system capable of generating sex-disaggregated data and conducting gender analysis for efficient administration, monitoring, and evaluation of social protection programs. Target date: 2025-12-31
